title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #14

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these plant parts is usually colourful? (1 mark)
   A. Flower
   B. Stem
   C. Root
   D. Soil

2. Which of these is a plant that has a thick main root with thin side roots? (1 mark)
   A. Grass
   B. Maize
   C. Bean plant
   D. Wheat

3. Which of these is a way that people benefit from plants? (1 mark)
   A. They cause floods
   B. They give food, shade and wood
   C. They give plastic
   D. They make noise

4. What should you do when you have a persistent stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Tell an adult and see a health worker
   C. Eat more sweets
   D. Drink dirty water

5. Where does the digestive tube begin? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Small intestine
   C. Stomach
   D. Anus

6. Why is diarrhoea dangerous for young children? (1 mark)
   A. They lose water quickly
   B. They sleep too much
   C. They become taller
   D. They grow more teeth

7. What is absorption? (1 mark)
   A. Swallowing food
   B. Digested food passing into the blood
   C. Chewing food
   D. Passing faeces

8. What happens to a gas that is put in a closed jar? (1 mark)
   A. It spreads to fill the whole jar
   B. It stays at the bottom
   C. It becomes a solid
   D. It sits at the top only

9. A kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same (1 mark)
   A. Volume
   B. Mass
   C. Colour
   D. Shape

10. Which of these can be a solid, liquid or gas depending on conditions? (1 mark)
   A. Stone
   B. Wooden chair
   C. Book
   D. Water

11. Which of these solids can be poured? (1 mark)
   A. Brick
   B. Flour
   C. Stone
   D. Ruler

12. A cup can hold about (1 mark)
   A. 25 ml
   B. 250 ml
   C. 25 litres
   D. 2500 ml

13. Steam from a boiling pot is really (1 mark)
   A. A white solid
   B. An invisible gas
   C. A red liquid
   D. A block of ice

14. Which is an example of reusing? (1 mark)
   A. Using a washed bottle to carry water
   B. Leaving it on the road
   C. Burning a plastic bottle
   D. Throwing it in a drain

15. Which waste is both decomposable and from an animal? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Tin
   C. Dung
   D. Glass

16. What should be done with stored rainwater before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Freeze it only
   B. Boil or treat it
   C. Drink it directly
   D. Add soil

17. How does mulching help save water? (1 mark)
   A. It makes water flow away
   B. It makes soil hot
   C. It makes soil dry
   D. It reduces evaporation from the soil

18. Which of these is an example of reducing water wastage? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving the hose on
   B. Closing a tap after use
   C. Washing with lots of water
   D. Ignoring leaks

19. Which of these is a way to save water when bathing? (1 mark)
   A. Use a sprinkler
   B. Leave the tap open
   C. Use a hose
   D. Use a basin

20. Why is saving water good for families? (1 mark)
   A. It makes water heavier
   B. It stops rain
   C. It causes floods
   D. It reduces the water bill

21. Which of these is a way of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. Closing taps
   B. Fixing leaks
   C. Using a bucket
   D. Leaving a tap running

22. Who should monitor taps in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody
   B. Only visitors
   C. Water monitors
   D. Only cooks

23. What should you do when doing force experiments? (1 mark)
   A. Keep fingers away from moving parts
   B. Run with sharp tools
   C. Push others
   D. Throw heavy things

24. Which of these is a way of reducing friction on a bicycle chain? (1 mark)
   A. Wetting it with mud
   B. Leaving it dry and rusty
   C. Adding sand
   D. Oiling it

25. A flat sheet of paper falls slower than a stone because (1 mark)
   A. Paper is bigger
   B. Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   C. Gravity does not pull paper
   D. The stone is bigger

26. Which of these is a push? (1 mark)
   A. Pulling a cart
   B. Kicking a football
   C. Drawing water with a rope
   D. Opening a drawer by its handle

27. Which of these can be a cheap way of lighting a house in a rural area? (1 mark)
   A. Many electric heaters
   B. Hundreds of candles
   C. Solar lamp
   D. A big generator

28. Which of these is translucent? (1 mark)
   A. Stone
   B. Wood
   C. Clear glass
   D. Tissue paper

29. Which of these is NOT a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. An electric bulb
   B. A mirror
   C. A candle
   D. A torch

30. Why are cooking pots made of metal? (1 mark)
   A. Metal is light
   B. Metal is soft
   C. Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   D. Metal does not get hot

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe the journey of a mouthful of food from the mouth to the anus. (4 marks)

32. Give two effects of force on objects. (2 marks)

33. Describe the function of each of these parts of a plant: roots, stem, leaves, flowers. (4 marks)

34. Explain the importance of conserving water at home and school. (5 marks)

35. Describe how you would measure 300 ml of water using a measuring jug, and how you would measure the mass of a mango. (5 marks)

36. Describe how to make a pair of kitchen gloves from local materials. (4 marks)

37. State two ways of reducing friction. (2 marks)

38. Explain why cooking pots are made of metal but their handles are not. (4 marks)

39. Write two uses of each of these: solids, liquids and gases. (Choose any four uses in all.) (4 marks)

40. A jug holds 500 ml of water. Musa pours in 250 ml and later takes out 100 ml. How much water is in the jug at the end? (4 marks)

41. Give three safety rules when using sources of light. (3 marks)

42. A jug has 1 litre of juice. 350 ml is poured into a cup. How much is left in the jug? (3 marks)

43. Name the part of a plant that makes food and the part that makes seeds. (2 marks)

44. List four water-saving habits that pupils can practise at school. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Flower
   Flowers are often brightly coloured.

2. C — Bean plant
   A bean plant has a main root with side roots. Maize and grass have many thin roots.

3. B — They give food, shade and wood
   Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood and clean air.

4. B — Tell an adult and see a health worker
   Adults and health workers can help find the cause.

5. A — Mouth
   Food enters the body through the mouth.

6. A — They lose water quickly
   The body loses a lot of water and can become weak.

7. B — Digested food passing into the blood
   Absorption means digested food parts pass into the blood.

8. A — It spreads to fill the whole jar
   A gas fills any container it is in.

9. B — Mass
   Both are 1 kg. The feathers take up much more space.

10. D — Water
   Water can be ice, liquid water or steam.

11. B — Flour
   Flour is made of tiny solid grains that can pour.

12. B — 250 ml
   A cup holds about 250 ml.

13. B — An invisible gas
   Steam is water as a gas and is invisible. The cloud we see is tiny water drops.

14. A — Using a washed bottle to carry water
   The bottle is used again for a new purpose.

15. C — Dung
   Animal dung rots and can be used as manure.

16. B — Boil or treat it
   Boiling or treating kills germs.

17. D — It reduces evaporation from the soil
   Covered soil stays moist longer.

18. B — Closing a tap after use
   Closing taps stops the flow of water.

19. D — Use a basin
   Using a basin limits the water used.

20. D — It reduces the water bill
   Less water used means less money paid.

21. D — Leaving a tap running
   A running tap that is not in use wastes water.

22. C — Water monitors
   Monitors help make sure taps are closed.

23. A — Keep fingers away from moving parts
   Safe practice prevents injuries.

24. D — Oiling it
   Oil helps parts slide.

25. B — Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   Air pushes up more on the wide flat sheet.

26. B — Kicking a football
   A kick pushes the ball.

27. C — Solar lamp
   Solar lamps use free energy from the sun.

28. D — Tissue paper
   Tissue paper lets some light through.

29. B — A mirror
   A mirror only reflects light.

30. C — Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   Metal passes heat from the fire to the food.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Chewed in the mouth, swallowed, pushed down the gullet, churned in the stomach, digested and absorbed in the small intestine, water taken back in the large intestine, faeces stored in the rectum and passed out of the anus.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for every two correct steps up to 4.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Change shape, start motion, stop motion, increase speed, decrease speed, change direction, hold things together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the plant and take in water. The stem supports the plant and carries water and food. Leaves make food. Flowers make fruits and seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: There is enough water for all, we save money, animals and crops get water, it reduces work of fetching water and protects sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason up to 5.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Place the jug on a flat surface, pour water until the level reaches the 300 mark with your eye level with the water. For the mango, place it on a balance and read the mass in grams.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for flat surface, pouring to 300 ml, eye level, using a balance, reading in grams.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose thick cotton cloth or old towel. Trace and cut two mitten shapes. Add an inner layer. Sew them together leaving the wrist open. Turn it inside out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smoothen surfaces, use oil or grease, use rollers, use ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Metal passes heat quickly to the food so it cooks. Handles made of wood or plastic pass heat slowly so our hands do not burn.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the pot and 2 marks for the handle.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: building, tools, clothes. Liquids: drinking, washing, cooking, fuel. Gases: breathing, cooking gas, inflating tyres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use up to 4.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 500 + 250 = 750, 1 mark for 750 - 100, 1 mark for 650, 1 mark for the unit ml.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never look directly at the sun, do not shine torches in eyes, keep candles and lamps away from curtains and paper, do not touch hot bulbs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1 litre = 1000 ml, 1 mark for the subtraction 1000 - 350 and 1 mark for the answer.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaves make food and flowers (fruits) make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, report leaks, use a bucket for watering the garden, water plants in the morning or evening, use a cup to drink.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
